item.title: Musk’s X Corp and SpaceXAI Resolve Antitrust Lawsuit Against Apple
item.description: Elon Musk’s X Corp and SpaceXAI said on Monday they have resolved their lawsuit in federal court in Texas that had accused Apple of conspiring to unlawfully monopolize markets for smartphones and generative AI chatbots. In a court filing, X and SpaceXAI moved to dismiss the lawsuit they brought against Apple last year. Related: Microsoft Joins AI Firms Calling for Caution With Cutting-Edge Models The lawsuit claimed Apple violated antitrust law by exclusively integrating ChatGPT into Apple Intelligence features on iPhones and other Apple devices.

item.title: Atlantic Hurricane Season Sets Record for Longest Without One
item.description: On Saturday, 2026 set a record for the longest a season has begun without a storm that has reached winds of 74 mph (119 kph) to qualify as a hurricane — at least in the satellite era, said Nick Novella, a meteorologist at the government’s Weather Prediction Center. The Atlantic is quiet — record quiet — this hurricane season thanks to an enormous El Niño that crushes storms before they get going. No Atlantic hurricanes have formed yet this year and none are likely to form for at least another week, even though this would normally be the peak of the season, according to the National Hurricane Center.

item.title: Microsoft Drafts Code of Conduct to Keep its AI Under Human Control
item.description: Microsoft on Monday unveiled a draft code of conduct for its in-house artificial intelligence that reflects growing industry concern that companies must keep future powerful AI under human control. “People matter more than AI,” Microsoft declared, in line with its prior vision for “humanist superintelligence.” The code of conduct represents a constitution of sorts for future models made by the company, Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman said in an interview with Reuters. The document, in the works for five to six months, would require Microsoft’s AI to never resist correction or shutdown, to communicate in ways that humans can understand, and to consider any conduct violation to be a failure — an effort to address concerns that AI can go to dangerous lengths to accomplish a task.

item.title: Upper Tribunal upholds Crispin Odey ban
item.description: Crispin Odey’s ban from the financial services industry has been upheld by the Upper Tribunal, which found he lacked integrity. The Tribunal considered Mr Odey’s attempted justifications for removing the ExCos to be no more than a smokescreen. Alongside the allegations arising directly from his dismissal of the ExCo's, the Tribunal upheld the allegations that Mr Odey’s dealings with OAM, its clients, its investors and the FCA lacked candour.

item.title: Premier Payment Solutions Ltd enters liquidation
item.description: On 10 September 2026, Premier Payment Solutions Ltd, which traded as PPS Money and MTBS (together, 'PPS Money'), entered liquidation. PPS Money is registered as a small payment institution under the Payment Services Regulations 2017 (the PSRs). The firm provided money-remittance services, primarily supporting money service businesses to make cross-border payments, including through its network of FCA-registered agents, which are businesses or individuals registered to provide payment services on its behalf.

item.title: Appleby secures growth investment from New Mountain Capital
item.description: Appleby, the specialist offshore law and corporate services provider with a significant insurance-linked securities practice, has secured a minority growth investment from affiliates of New Mountain Capital, in a move that is set to accelerate the law firm’s growth strategy. Under the terms of the agreement, New Mountain, a growth-oriented investment firm with roughly $60 billion in assets under management, will take a minority interest in a newly established company in the Cayman Islands that will indirectly hold Appleby Global Group LLC. New Mountain’s investment positions the firm to expand into new jurisdictions and service lines, further invest in technology and innovation, and enhance client service” Moller continued: “We are pleased New Mountain recognizes Appleby’s pre-eminent positioning and growth opportunity, and are excited to partner with an investor that has a long track record of supporting fast growing professional services organizations.”

item.title: CalPERS ramps up cat bond and ILS investments to near $2.5bn valuation at mid-year 2026
item.description: CalPERS, the largest public pension fund in the United States, has continued to expand its investments in catastrophe bond and insurance-linked securities fund strategies with the combined valuation of its allocations to the asset class nearing $2.5 billion at the mid-point of 2026, an increase of around 70% just in the first-half of this year. Disclosures made as of the end of last year showed that CalPERS ILS investments reached a valuation of $1.451 billion as of December 31st 2025, as it continued to allocate to these managers. But now, the latest CalPERS documents seen by Artemis show that the level of investment allocation across the three ILS fund access points was actually much higher still, with the total valuation of the ILS investments rising further through the first-half of 2026.

item.title: Dave Przesiek named President & CEO of Ryan Specialty Benefits
item.description: Ryan Specialty, a specialty insurance intermediary, has announced the appointment of Dave Przesiek as President & Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Ryan Specialty Benefits, its Benefits division. Przesiek succeeds John Zern, who leaves Ryan Specialty Benefits following nearly six years with the company to pursue other interests. Pat Ryan, Executive Chairman of Ryan Specialty, commented, “We thank John for his services and wish him well in his future endeavours.” Przesiek brings more than 30 years of experience in the health and benefits industry.

item.title: Loss of senior underwriting expertise tops AI replacement fears, hx finds
item.description: Commercial insurance underwriters fear losing senior expertise more than being replaced by artificial intelligence (AI), yet firms are investing least in preserving that knowledge, according to a recent hyperexponential (hx) survey. It surveyed 350 Chief Underwriting Officers, Heads of Underwriting / Line of Business, and Senior and Lead Underwriters working in commercial and specialty Property & Casualty insurance, split 43% UK and 57% US. Furthermore, just 12% of senior and lead underwriters feel AI is fully integrated into their workflow, compared to 29% of Chief Underwriting Officers, showing confidence grows further from the actual work.

item.title: Record Diesel Prices Come at a Bad Time for U.S. Farmers
item.description: The price of diesel is hitting record highs just when many U.S. American diesel prices are now 60% higher than they were before the U.S. Prices quickly climbed as the cost of crude oil — the main ingredient in diesel, as well as gasoline — skyrocketed amid disruptions to tanker traffic in the Strait of Hormuz because of the war.

item.title: Brown & Riding Launches Agribusiness Practice
item.description: Brown & Riding announced the launch of its new national Agribusiness Practice, a specialty practice area delivering comprehensive insurance solutions for the entire agricultural supply chain. The Agribusiness Practice helps retail agents deliver customized solutions for farm, food, and agriculture-oriented operations, including custom farming, dairies, nuts, and more; premises with various operations that have a public exposure, including liquor exposures; seed and grain processing mills; poultry and meat producers; processing, packing, and storage facilities; agricultural machinery and equipment manufacturing, distribution, and rental; ground and aerial chemical applicators; and logistics and transportation of agricultural products, as well as various other risks. The practice is led by David Chipp, and supported by a team of product line specialists with deep technical expertise and market access, providing sophisticated coverage solutions for food and agricultural clients.

item.title: World Insurance Associates Acquires Texas’ Cubriel

item.title: US Declares End of Largest Recorded Cyclosporiasis Outbreak
item.description: health authorities on Friday declared the nation’s largest recorded multistate cyclosporiasis outbreak over, after contaminated iceberg lettuce sickened thousands, though the FDA said it was still probing how the parasite entered the food supply. The outbreak, which federal investigators linked to lettuce from central Mexico sourced by Taylor Farms, prompted one of the largest food recalls in recent years and renewed scrutiny of food-safety controls for imported produce. Related: US Widens Lettuce-Related Cyclosporiasis Probe to 20 States According to data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, 12,883 people across 21 states fell ill after consuming contaminated lettuce.

item.title: Arizona Accuses L’Oreal of Concealing Cancer Risks Linked to Hair Relaxers
item.description: Arizona Attorney General Kristin Mayes, a Democrat, filed the lawsuit late Thursday in state court, making Arizona the first state to sue over alleged cancer risks linked to hair relaxers. The lawsuit accuses L’Oreal of violating state consumer protection laws by marketing the products, which are used predominantly by African American women, without warning consumers about the alleged risks of ovarian and uterine cancers. subsidiary, alleging the cosmetics company hid evidence that its hair relaxer products could cause cancer in women, as it faces thousands of similar lawsuits from users and their families.

item.title: Reviewing Your AI Tools at 3, 6, and 12 Months: A Framework for Sustaining and Scaling
item.description: View Series Six months after a claims team goes live with an AI tool, someone asks a simple question in a leadership meeting: is it still doing what we bought it to do? The months after launch rarely get the same rigor, often with adoption left to happen naturally, rather than managed as deliberately as the initial rollout plan. That’s why it’s worth treating the first year as a series of checkpoints: At this stage, you might still be working through implementation or customizing the solution to your workflow , but there should be some initial usage data to compare the designed workflow against what you actually have.

item.title: Dead Weight On The Cap Table: The Startup Equity Problem Causing Litigation And How You Can Fix It
item.description: By the time a founder leaves or gets terminated, the damage is already done, leaving the company stuck with costly “dead weight on the cap table.” When a co-founder with substantial ownership leaves — voluntarily or involuntarily — they often walk away with a massive, permanent piece of the company. Yet almost no one talks about how this default framework routinely causes bitter legal battles over founder equity, wasting hundreds of thousands of dollars on litigation that could have been avoided. From a VC’s perspective, and that of the remaining partners, this is pure dead weight.

item.title: Swiss Re highlights growing catastrophe protection gap as nat cat losses rise 5-7% annually
item.description: Reinsurance giant Swiss Re has highlighted how growing natural catastrophe risk remains a significant driver of reinsurance demand, as insured nat cat losses continue to follow a 5–7% annual growth rate, driven by increasing exposures, rising asset values and changing hazard patterns. Crucially, this rise in societal exposure underscores an expanding catastrophe protection gap, as well as a growing need for broader risk transfer solutions. At the 68th annual meeting of the reinsurance industry in Monte Carlo, Swiss Re shared that its modelling indicates that insured losses could reach around US $320 billion in a 2026 peak loss scenario, which clearly demonstrates the value of reinsurance protection against low-frequency, high-severity events.

item.title: 28% of reinsurance buyers expect to increase alternative capital use in 2027: Moody’s
item.description: For the insurance-linked securities (ILS) market, one of the most promising findings of Moody’s Ratings annual survey of reinsurance buyers is that 28% of respondents said they anticipate increased use of alternative capital sources in 2027. “Among respondents, 28% expect to increase their use of alternative capital in 2027, while the remainder expect it to remain unchanged.” The rating agency also asks buyers whether they have a preference for specific types of alternative capital structures and protection. It might imply buyers see significant value in alternative capital at this stage of the cycle, in allowing them to lock-in mostly longer-duration reinsurance and retrocession covers in structured formats.

item.title: Arch Re promoted Roberts to Head of ILS, hired Neyme as ILS Portfolio Manager
item.description: Arch Re, the global reinsurance arm of Arch Capital group, has promoted Christian Roberts as its new Head of ILS and hired Cyril Neyme as an ILS Portfolio Manager, with both of these moves happening in July this year. With Roberts moving up to become Head of ILS, we understand Arch Re hired a new portfolio manager for its insurance-linked securities activities around the same time. We understand that Roberts’ direct manager Allan Voltz had been promoted to lead the Arch US mortgage insurance division, after which the company opted to promote Roberts and put him in place its first Head of Insurance-Linked Securities within its reinsurance division.

item.title: Huxley to succeed Besemer as FOIL CEO
item.description: The Forum of Insurance Lawyers (FOIL), a professional UK membership organisation established in 1992 that represents lawyers defending insurance-related claims, has a ppointed Mark Huxley as its new Chief Executive Officer, effective October 1, 2026. Huxley, a renowned insurance professional, will be succeeding Laurence Besemer, who is moving on to pursue other ventures and consultancy projects within the insurance industry. According to the announcement, Besemer will stay at FOIL until the end of the calendar year to ensure a smooth handover to his successor.

item.title: Ford to Recall About 223,500 Vehicles Over Fuel Tank Issues
item.description: Ford is recalling 223,472 vehicles in the U.S. due to leaky and improperly secured fuel tanks that may detach from the vehicle while driving, the U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said on Saturday.

item.title: Fayed Abuse Victims Seek Up to £150 Million From Harrods
item.description: After years denying women’s accounts about his abuse, Harrods said in a statement in 2024 that it was “utterly appalled by the allegations” and was “determined to do the right thing.” The retailer created its own compensation plan for Fayed’s victims in March last year, saying it thought the offer was attractive for victims as they would not have to pay additional legal fees. Almost 300 women who say they were sexually abused by former Harrods owner Mohamed Al Fayed want as much as £150 million ($203 million) in compensation from the luxury department store, more than double the amount it’s set aside. The £62 million provision Harrods made in 2024 for redress payments will fall well short of what’s required, according to KP Law, which represents about 275 people, most of whom are former employees.

item.title: New Attacks in Hormuz and Saudi Test Nerves as War’s Spread Worsens Oil Disruption
item.description: New strikes on Saudi Arabia and on ships in the Gulf tested nerves in the Middle East on Sunday, after an attack on a Saudi oil pipeline and an advance by Yemen’s Houthis threatened to worsen the wartime disruption to global energy supplies. Southern Saudi cities have experienced regular alerts since last week, culminating in drone strikes on Friday that knocked out the 1,200-km (745-mile) east-west pipeline across the Arabian Peninsula that has served as the main route for global supplies of Middle East oil bypassing the Strait of Hormuz. After that, as much as 4% of global oil supply could be jeopardized, on top of the millions of barrels a day already lost to the disruption to traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Nina Arquint named President, Commercial, EMEA of Allianz Commercial and AGCS
item.description: Allianz Commercial, the corporate insurance division of Allianz Group, has announced the appointment of Nina Arquint as President, Commercial, Europe, Middle East and Africa (EMEA) of Allianz Commercial and Allianz Global Corporate & Specialty (AGCS), effective 1 April 2027. Arquint will join the AGCS Board of Management and will report to Thomas Lillelund, chief executive officer of Allianz Commercial. In her new role, she will be responsible for Allianz Commercial’s Large Corporate (LargeCorp) and Mid Corporate (MidCorp) business across EMEA.

item.title: Insurance Risks Losing Expertise to Retirements
item.description: The insurance industry's persistent talent crunch goes far deeper than a hiring gap – it's also becoming a knowledge gap, as the accumulated judgment of a workforce built over decades retires faster than it can be replaced. Bureau of Labor Statistics estimates roughly 400,000 insurance professionals will have retired in the last half-decade alone. Today's average insurance employee is in their mid-40s to mid-50s, depending on the line of business.

The app can collect and confirm pet details, present factual plan information, adjust quote options, and answer questions about Lassie’s coverage and policy terms.
